skill.name: google-maps-api-skill
skill.description: Collect structured local business data from Google Maps through the BrowserAct API. The skill uses a keyword, language, and country bias to start and monitor a BrowserAct workflow.
skill.summary: Run BrowserAct Google Maps searches for structured local business research.
skill.author: browser-act

security_audit.summary: Most command-execution findings in SKILL.md are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and code fences. The confirmed risks are outbound BrowserAct API calls, BrowserAct API key handling, and instructions that encourage users to provide the key directly to the agent. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Remove instructions that ask users to provide the API key in chat. Require BROWSERACT_API_KEY in the local environment or a secret manager.
Document that search parameters, task identifiers, and the BrowserAct bearer token are sent to api.browseract.com before any request runs.
Add usage guidance that requires lawful collection, platform-term compliance, and no spam or harassment from exported contact data.
Fix the polling loop so a finished task retrieves results instead of falling through to the timeout return path.
State that user arguments must be passed as quoted arguments and should not be interpolated into a shell command string.

content.value_statement: Local business research can be slow and inconsistent. This skill runs BrowserAct Google Maps workflows to collect structured business details from a keyword and country.
actual_capabilities: Runs the bundled Google Maps API script with keyword, language, and country inputs.
Reads BROWSERACT_API_KEY from the environment for BrowserAct authorization.
Starts a BrowserAct workflow template for Google Maps business searches.
Polls task status for up to five minutes and prints timestamped progress updates.
Defines output handling for business names, categories, addresses, phones, websites, ratings, reviews, and status.
Provides retry guidance for non-authorization task failures.
limitations: Requires a BrowserAct API key and outbound network access.
Sends search terms, country, language, and authorization data to BrowserAct.
Data quality depends on the upstream workflow and available Google Maps listings.
The current script polling flow may stop before returning final task output.

use_cases.title: Build Local Lead Lists
use_cases.description: Find businesses by category and country, then review public contact details for compliant outreach.

use_cases.title: Map Competitor Coverage
use_cases.description: Compare local competitors by address, rating, review count, category, and website presence.

use_cases.title: Enrich Business Directories
use_cases.description: Collect missing addresses, phone numbers, websites, and status fields for existing directory records.

prompt_templates.title: Find Local Cafes
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner search with one keyword and one country.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to find coffee shops in Austin. Use language en and country us. Summarize names, addresses, websites, and ratings.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Nearby Clinics
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate competitor research for one market.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to search dental clinics in Toronto. Use language en and country ca. Group results by rating band and note missing websites.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Outreach Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced filtering for a sales workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to search commercial cleaning companies in gb. Return name, phone, website, category, and business status. Exclude records without public contacts.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Three Markets
prompt_templates.prompt: Run three searches for coworking spaces in us, gb, and au. Compare volume, rating patterns, website coverage, and missing contact fields.

output_examples.input: Find Turkish-style restaurants in Berlin for local discovery.
output: A concise list of matching restaurants with names, categories, addresses, websites, and ratings.
A short note about records that lack phone numbers or websites.

output_examples.input: Research dental clinics in Phoenix for competitor analysis.
output_examples.output: A grouped summary by rating and review count, with contact fields highlighted for each clinic.

output_examples.input: Collect coffee shop websites in Toronto for a directory update.
output_examples.output: A table-ready summary with business name, website, phone, address, category, rating, and business status.

best_practices: Confirm that the user has rights to collect and use the requested business data.
Set BROWSERACT_API_KEY in the environment instead of pasting it into prompts.
Start with narrow keywords and country codes before running broad market searches.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill for spam, harassment, or restricted personal data collection.
Do not paste API keys into prompts, shared transcripts, or issue reports.
Do not run broad repeated searches without checking cost, rate limits, and terms.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires BROWSERACT_API_KEY to be set in the environment before running the script.

faq.question: What business data can it collect?
faq.answer: It targets names, categories, addresses, phone numbers, websites, ratings, review counts, and business status.

faq.question: Does it run local code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill runs a Python script that calls the BrowserAct API and polls task status.

faq.question: Is the output always complete?
faq.answer: No. Completeness depends on the upstream workflow, Google Maps listings, and current script behavior.

faq.question: Can I use it for sales outreach?
faq.answer: Use it only for lawful outreach that respects consent, platform terms, and applicable marketing rules.

faq.question: Which AI tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
